hypotheses.title: Compare touch, candle confirmation and H1 context
hypotheses.signal: Pivots left=3/right=3 available only after right confirmation. BOS is first completed close past latest unbroken pivot. Require BOS candle abs(close-open)/ATR14(previous completed bar)>=1. Zone is full range of last opposite candle among 10 pre-BOS bars; known at BOS close. Invalidate on completed close beyond far edge; expires 96 M15 bars; first touch only. A: resting order at near edge from next bar; B: touch followed by first directional candle close within next 3 bars, next-open entry; C: B plus last completed H1 structure direction matches and H1 close above/below EMA50. One entry per zone. Stop far edge +/-0.1 prior ATR14; target 1.5R; stop-first ambiguous bars; close after 32 M15 bars if unexited.
hypotheses.baseline: A touch with identical zones, stops, costs and periods; evaluate B-A and C-B as two comparisons.
hypotheses.notes: No implementation here. 1R and 2R are deferred hypotheses, not hidden additional trials. Max one open position for comparable opportunity accounting.

hypotheses.title: Session differences at first retest
hypotheses.signal: Apply frozen B from H01. Classify fill by Asia/Tokyo 09-18, Europe/London 08-17, America/New_York 08-17 local time. Overlap is separate, not duplicated in independent groups. Compare sessions on net R with identical execution and weekday controls.
hypotheses.baseline: All-session B; report London-only and New-York-only differences, overlaps separately.
hypotheses.notes: Session boundaries fixed before testing; no test-set session optimization.

hypotheses.title: Relative futures volume and volatility context
hypotheses.signal: Exploratory only: B with current completed confirmation-bar volume / mean(previous 20 same-source bars)>=1.5; separately describe prior ATR14/close terciles from development data. Do not label either feature OFI, aggressor direction or market depth.
hypotheses.notes: Use actual provider futures volume separately from broker tick counts. Gold trade-aggressor/depth hypothesis blocked until timestamped quotes/trades are obtained.

hypotheses.title: Weekly managed-money positioning extremes
hypotheses.signal: At first completed daily bar after verified COT availability, label current managed-money net below prior-156-report 10th percentile or above 90th percentile, with >=104 prior reports; evaluate signed next-5-trading-day return in contrarian direction. Overlapping weekly horizons purged. Use one fixed horizon; archives with retrieval-only timing cannot support historical release tests.
hypotheses.baseline: Unconditional next-5-day return matched by weekday and sample; trend-following interpretation is a separate future trial.
hypotheses.notes: Require >=10 years of daily gold futures, verified publication/vintage audit and sufficient extreme events; 30 per tail is only a pilot floor, not significance. Raw net can drift with open interest; normalization is a separate registered future hypothesis.

hypotheses.title: Zone rule against a simple momentum baseline
hypotheses.signal: Compare frozen B against next-open entry after a directional M15 candle with abs(close-open)/prior ATR14>=1, no zone requirement. Match direction, session and volatility strata using development-only weights; baseline stop distance 1 prior ATR14, target 1.5R, max hold32.
hypotheses.notes: Zone benefit cannot be inferred from trades alone without an opportunity benchmark. No credible direct evidence for hidden orders in these candle patterns was established in this review.

hypotheses.title: Execution-cost robustness
hypotheses.signal: Apply H01 variants with verified venue spread, commission and slippage; stress total per-side costs at 1x,1.5x,2x without changing entries. Touch-fill sensitivity must include gaps, adverse selection and uncertain same-bar path; do not claim exact fills from M15 OHLC.
hypotheses.baseline: Same signals at measured 1x costs; zero-cost results diagnostic only.
hypotheses.notes: No broker specs are currently set. Dollar sizing or realistic CFD P&L remains blocked. These are stress scenarios, not a search for the best multiplier.
